text: Our first official dart is tossed at whoever decided to move campus police off campus. And what's wllh that new name ... Public Safety Office? What the hell Is that?

And what could be more deserving of our first official pat than the return of the mushroom! (Wild Applause). It may be In a different place and it may be the wrong color, but hey, at least you can petition something and get results. Ouch.

How many freshmen can you cram Into an Interstate-side hotel? Try 90 in HoJo·s. We give the administration a big dart for making poor freshman souls go through that again. Let"s see that's $6.000 a semester ... about $52 a night ... and that even Includes an education.
Double pat to the completed construction of the new Business Building and Burruss Hall. Poor Burruss -all that for ... that?

Ho hum, zippity doe, where did all the parking go? A nice fat dart flies at whoever decided to convert P-lot (originally designated for commuter parking) to a faculty/staff parking lot. Changing S-lot behind Anthony-Seeger from faculty/staff to commuter is hardly a fair trade-off.
A cool pat to D-Hall for turning on the air-conditioning this semester.
That'll be $5,236.95 ... please. "Jeez and the book's used!"
Repeatable pats to Food Services for the free R-mugs distributed this week. The reusable receptacles really rallied recycling reformers.

What's up with these campus phones? Double dart to the Cerebus company who's responsible for the serious 5 p.m. phone glitch. There's a suspicious consistency to these nightly melt downs. This wouldn't have anything to do with it being free registration time now, would it?
No more dusty eyeballs and rock-filled teeth between Cleveland and Miller Halls. One immense pat goes to campus construction for paving the gravel pit between these two buildings.

A sympathetic and admirable pat goes to the freshmen who brave the humiliation of wandering through Carrier Library with their English 101 library guides. Just think, one day you too will be able to put in hours and hours of searching for material our library just doesn't consider necessary for the 21st century.

Gettin' nothin' but static, genin' nothin' but static, genin' nothin' but static on my dorm T.V. Darts galore to the administration for promising cable television in Bluestone dorms and not following through with it. Now everybody on campus has to hang out at the villiage if they want to watch something other than "Wild Kingdom" behind a curtain of fuzz.
Another pat to D-hall for "picnic day." Taking your dinner out to feast on the hill was a nice change of pace.

What a funny thing, why didn't the paper come out on Monday and why were we in classes? Because for some reason JMU, unlike the Americans who print our paper, does not recognize Labor Day-the national holiday that recognizes all those who slave week after week to maintain the tax-operated government we all know and love. Double dart to anyone responsible for us not having our own slave-free day.
Pats to the return of the recycling bins on main campus. Now there are no excuses for just trashing your bottles and cans-throw them in the white-topped receptacles!

A heat-seeking dart goes to whoever is in charge of dorm furnishings. Hate to rag on the administration again, but it would seem that a couch or two to rest one's throbbing hide after a long day of classes isn't too much to ask for. Hats off to the comrades of Ikenberry who have braved their empty suites for the second week in a row. This Dart was sent in by one Mr. Matt Barnay of Ikenberry. Hang in there Matt.
If you haven't tried them, you don't know what you're missing. A scrumptious pat goes to PC Dukes for continuing to tantalize our taste buds with those other-worldly chocolate chip cookies . . .

. . . But who said anyone was perfect. We launch a dart right back at PC Dukes for the mystery mist that comes out of that chimney thing. What is that stuff? Anti-gravitational grease? Maybe you should install some scrubbers on that stack so as to eliminate some of that industrial burger waste - if that's what it is.

A very intelligent pat goes to Carrier Library, who has begun to fight for greater access with a fax program. If you can't find a journal entry, and the journal is available at certain other libraries, the library will fax it to you. FREE. in a DAY. In a world of shrinking budgets, you can't ask for more.

An academic dart flies at Carrier Library for pulling that Sunday stunt of opening at 2:00 p.m. and then closing at 10:00 p.m. Yeah it was the end of the first week and all, but it's imperative for students to have some place quiet to go and think about how their work is piling up.

An annoyed dart files at D-hall for the recent influx of flies. Opening the windows instead of using a perfectly-functioning AC unit is obviously the problem here. Energy efficiency is good, but not when the sacrifice is changing an indoor dining experience into a Fourth of July picnickin' fly-fest, let alone a health hazard.
But a thoughtful pat to D-hall for their soon-to-be-a-reality veggie line. Yes! More than just salads for the rest of the semester.

An expensive dart flies at whoever decided to up the price of dorm washers to 75 cents. 75 cents a load? Plus all the quarters you have to pump into those dryers that just don't dry? Sent in by Jen Horan.
Lots of "Ooooo's" and "Aaaaah's" to the administration and the Daily News-Record for the awesome fireworks display Saturday.
target: the administration and the Daily News-Record

text: A dart of punctuality flies at the bus system for running 20 minutes late on Thursday. Professor: "Tardy again Mr. Doe?" Student: "My bus was late sir, sorry." Professor: "Oh shut up and sit down you insolent little punk. And I suppose the dog at your homework."
A healthy pat goes to the Health Center for hiring a new doctor. Welcome aboard to Dr. Diana Jensen. Happy healing!
A dull dart to whoever forgot to put pencil sharpeners in the business building.

A thank you pat to JMU President Ronald Carrier for meeting with the Council for Campus Leaders on Sept. 9. Thanks fr the support, Uncle Ron. Sent in by Janet Driscoll, President of Circle K International.

A congested dart flies at whoever is in charge of bicycle rack installation on campus. Sidewalk chains and railings as well as trees, benches and posts only go so far. There are more bikes on campus this semester than ever before - a little adaptation would be appreciated.

A hardy pat goes to Burger King for their football score/percentage off meal plan. If you missed it, here's the scoop: The people at Burger King vowed to turn the number f points the Dukes scored into a percentage discount off their meal cmbo. And we got 49 percent off!!! Now that's a bargain.
A soggy dart to campus grounds crew for strategically placing sprinklers across sidewalks so that everybody gets soaked.
Oops. How could we forget the Dukes? The only reason that Burger King bargain was so enjoyable was because of them. Burgers and fries galore to the Dukes for scoring 49 big ones and slaughtering UCF!

A lost dart to the designers of the business building for making a beautiful but confusing building more bewildering by having no information center, not even an office on the entry level or a directory. Help! We business students are smart, but c'mon! Sent in by an unidentified business student.

To The Breeze for increasing awareness about rape and sexual abuse ("Familiarity and Contempt" and "Sharing the Sexual Burden." Keep it up! Even though many people may believe they have heard enough and consider themselves aware, it is obvious that some still have much to learn. Sent in by graduate student Laura Vorst.

But a double dart to The Breeze for not covering all the JMU students abroad and depcting Germany as still being divided in its Aug. 29 issue. Sent in by senior Brad Burch. Knew we couldn't get away with just a pat.

An applauding pat to the UPB for having sme really cool movies and programs already this semester. Talk about diversity - Pee Wee Herman and "Henry and June" - can't wait for the censorship symposium next semester.
A light-spirited dart to the ghost of Carrier Library for scuplting the mysterious 13 in the stacks on Friday. Unlucky for the library staff, but kind of funny anyway.

A well-deserved pat to the Office of Public Safety (a.k.a. campus police) and the campus cadets for their conveinent and comforting late-night escort service. It's nice to know there is always someone to call for help.
target: the Office of Public Safety (a.k.a. campus police) and the campus cadets

text: A peaceful dart goes to The Breeze for using the Mercedes Benz symbol instead of the peace sign once on the front page of the Sept. 16 issue, and five times on pages 14 and 15 of the same issue. Sent in by Erin Goewey and housemates.

A rhythmic pat to Full Stop for gracing the commons yesterday with some chillin' music mon. If you weren't there, you missed a great show under a great sky. As a matter of fact it was just the way a thumpin' reggae show ought to be.

Not that it's D-hall's fault, but we'll dart 'em anyway for the ungodly length of the food lines lately. Something is definitely up when, for instance, lines two and three are so mixed due to overcrowding that it's hard to tell where each line begins. Maybe installing some cattle railing is the way of the future.
A tasty, chewy, cream-cheese-filled pat to Mr. Chips for adding Mr. J's bagels to their stock. They sure make 9 o'clocks delectable.

A sweaty, drippy dart goes to the unbearably hot weather we've been having lately. Why do Harrisonburg City kids get out early because of heat and we don't? The forecast calls for cooler temperatures, but of course we can expect cloudy skies and rain as well. Maybe Mother Nature is preparing us for another unpredictable winter.
A healthy pat goes to the Health Center and the new women's health center that is set to open by mid-semester and be in full operation by the spring.
target: the Health Center and the new women's health center

text: A wasteful dart for the sprinkler demonstratioin last week. A gardening tip - try not to water your lawn during the hottest hours of the day. The mid-day showers were refreshing and we know Parent's Weeken is coming up, but let's be reasonable.
A chillin' pat to this great autumn weather. Someone in a very high place finally decided to pull the plug on the 'ole heat lamp. Cool man.

A nasty dart to anyone who, instead of photocopying or just taking notes from journals like a normal person, actually rips out the pages. That leaves everyone else without a source. It is just a tad frustrating to discover some neanderthal has destroyed a journal you spent days searching for in Carrier Library.
Well, D-Hall does it again. A patriotic pat to this semester's grand opening of American Pie. Burgers and fries but hey, where's the apple pie?

A dead-end dart for closing off the road between Spotswood and Johnston to thru traffic. Traffic jams galore, especially when you're dodging bikes, U-turning cars, and the monster tractors still plowing around Burruss.
Sugar-sweet pats to UPB for providing ice-cream and toppings for the make-your-own sundae, bring-your-own banana fest last Thursday at Dukes.
A thick-skulled dart to the neanderthals who refuse to use their R-mugs - get a conscience. Sent in by John Fennel & David Harrington.

A cordial pat to JMU's Student Ambassadors for hosting the Class of '56 Reunion on campus over the weekend. May all of you who volunteered your time be met with the same youthful enthusiasm upon returning for your own class reunion.

In the continuing sprinkler saga, a soggy dart to the party responsible for watering the business building and Johnston Hall lawns during the rainstorm Monday. Rain is a natural phenomenon where lots of water falls fro m the sky, which means natural water for the grass. The budget belt is tight enough - let's not tempt the state into turning our water off too.

A delectable pat to the Steak House for increasing the size of their steaks. Maybe this will encourage students to show up on time for their reservations since a grace period of 10 minutes is no longer permitted.
Do we have a water theme here? What happened to the Everpure Water in D-Hall? A drip-dry dart to this sputtering liquid that has a knack for running out at the precise moment anybody wants to use it.

A tolerant pat to JMU's full- and part-time faculty members for hanging in there during these critical times. It's often said that "students ar the future" but what kind of future would any of us have without the concern and patience all of you possess?
target: JMU's full- and part-time faculty members

text: An anonymous dart flies at people who sit out in the commons, microphone in hand, and badger people for money. Of course, this was all done in "good fun" but just remember not everyone has the same toleration for "fun." Don't worry — we won't mention any names.

Due to a sharp decrease in Darts and Pats submissions we have been forced to pat the weather again. The weather this weekend ended a string of gray days - a little meteorological variety is always nice. Yeah right, please send in more Darts and Pats.

A contradictory dart flies at whoever confused the times for faculty parking lots to open for students. The handbook says lots open at 4 p.m. but the signs say 5 p.m. Someone called The Breeze with this dart and has already received a ticket because of this discrepancy. Someone needs to fix the typo in the handbook or repaint the sign.
A photogenic pat to the photographers who have agreed to photograph the entire student body for the yearbook - or at least the students who sign up.

But an annoyed dart flies at the same photographers who, even though they're just doing their job, make you feel like a complete idiot by placing you in the most unnatural poses and then saying, "yeah, that's the one. You look marvelous."
A victorious pat to the football team for putting William and Mary under. Close game, but like they always say, "It ain't over 'til it's over."

A thieving dart to the people who steal newspapers off residence hall porches. We pay for those and some of us read them for classes. Just because we don't get there at 8 a.m. to pick them up, doesn't mean you're entitled to them. They're only 25 cents - get your own! Sent in by a seething morning-edition subscriber.

An involved pat to the crowd of students who listenend to and participated in the pro-choice debate on the Commons Tuesday night No matter what your views are on the subject, thanks for getting involved in the issues around you. Sent in by a concerned citizen.

A disgusting dart to all the people who pick up food from the sald bars, sniff it, and then return it to the salad bars. People, that has got to be one of the most disgusting things I have witnessed in my four years here at JMU. Sent in by a grossed-out, salad-eating senior.

An innovative pat to the implementation of a bus route from Hoffman Hall to the Business Building. The bus route is quite convenient, well-used and even on time. Thanks! Sent in by a bus-riding business student.

A blinded dart flies at the person who decided to put tenn-wat light bulbs in the ceiling lights in Gifford Hall. The celings are already 20 feet above us and now we need about three or four personal lamps to get a decent amount of illumination in the rooms. Sent in by a Gifford resident afraid of going blind.
sender: a Gifford resident afraid of going blind

text: Mucho pats to all who submitted Darts and Pats this week. Keep 'em rolling in!

A cool pat to all community businesses, such as Chevron and Food-Mart, for honoring JMU's EARTH mug and R-mug. We're happy to pat those JMU students who really are using their mugs on and off campus. We can save the world! Well, at least it's a good start.

D-d-d-dart. Catch a clue, it wasn't the tin man who was in search of a brain! It was the scarecrow! Education under Wilder is sad indeed! Sent in by a group identified as "the gals from Suite I." Hmm. The edit. cartoon ran Sept. 30.
sender: a group identified as "the gals from Suite I

text: A mercy pat to all who continue to read The Breeze despite brainless cartoons such as Trevor the Tree Frog. What's the point? Certainly not humor. Ouch. Sent in by Paul Devine.

A behemothic dart to whoever decided that Y-Lot for commuters does not need to be paved. At the end of the day, not only did I not recognize my brown car, which was black when I parked it, but when I tried to leave, my car did not budge in that gravel booby trap. Sent in by Tammy Rinehart, who also wanted to pat the campus police and cadets for pushing her car out of the gravel depths of Y-Lot.

And an annoyed dart to whoever made the decision to change E-Lot temporarily to commuter parking. Since the lot will only be open a short time, why bother? Well, we think something is better than nothing, but the commuter who sent this in seems a bit perturbed by the whole affair.
A hearty pat to all who've given blood in the past two weeks. Talk about saving the world.
An artistic dart to Sawhill Gallery for displaying a ceramic penis. Sent in by an offended art critic.
A thankful pat to the Student Ambassadors for their help in making Parents' Weekend such a success! Sent in by University Advancement.

A flaming dart shot at D-hall for allowing their employees to smoke in the dining area. Some students would like to breathe while eating their meals. Please, there is enough pollution in the air as it is. Sent in by a very concerned student who doesn't want lung cancer.

A party hearty pat to UPB for offering JMU students a true spring break adventure. For the first time, the organization is sponsoring a trip to New Orleans during Mardi Gras 1992. What an artsy, jazzy, groovy idea.

An impatient dart goes to Food Services for delaying the opening of Lifeline in favor of American Pie. We JMU vegetarians realize the desire some have for cow sandwiches, but come on, we're starving. Baked potatoes and salads only go so far. Sent in by frustrated members of the JMU vegetarian population. The vegetarian line will open Oct. 21.
sender: frustrated members of the JMU vegetarian population

text: But we'd like to pat Food Services for the effort to implement a vegetarian entree at the Steak House. Hopefully, it won't be only vegetable lasagna. But anything is better than double onion rings on a date.

A misguided dart at whoever is responsible for getting the permanent telephone books out. Sent in by a commuter student who wonders how much longer off-campus students will have to guess at phone numbers.
A literary pat to the Green Valley Book Fair. For the bookworms on campus, it was two weekends of pure pleasure — cheap books, and plenty of 'em.

A tree-hugging dart to all the overly emphatic environmentalists who have jumped on the bandwagon by viewing the planet as superior to its most advanced inhabitants. Just because some of us don't share your affections for dirt and bark does not make us mindless or heartless. Get off our backs about your R-mugs. Sent in by Marl L. McKinney, John J. Downey and Jonathan Deloatch who label themselves as "students more concerned with urban decay."
A soothing pat to Mrs. Green's for playing music during breakfast. Sent in by a relaxed Mrs. Green' breakfast-goer.

A sloppy dart to whoever fills the drink machine in Wilson breezeway. Either put bigger cups in the machine or turn down the dispenser. Sent in by a person who's tired of having Coke drip all over everything.
A pretty pat to all the beautiful flowers on campus. Sent in by a parent.

A dart to the JMU campus police. A printer was stolen from Shenandoah Hall? The office of public safety? C'mon! Students living on campus must really feel as though their property is safe. Sent in by senior Johnny Bau.

A triumphant pat to the Washington Redskins for their undefeated reign this season. Go Skins! Though of course, if Baltimore had a team, it would no doubt be kicking the skin out of Washington. Sent in by a loyal Baltimore resident forced to pick a team, any team.

A disgusting dart to all who allow students to enter any eating facility without any shoes. Yes, students have to be fed, but should it be at the expense of other students worrying about germs? I propose that they should adopt a basic policy — no shoes, no food! Sent in by a disturbed and grossed out D-Hall employee.
sender: a disturbed and grossed out D-Hall employee

text: A super-spirited pat to the "Bum the Eagles Bonfire" this Friday on Hillside field. Gosh, this is just like the movies.

Yet another apathetic dart to those who are too lazy or close-minded to clip a free mug onto their backpacks to save money and resources. Sent in by Nicholas McDowell, a non-tree-hugging concerned student who doesn't eat bark.
A resourceful pat to Dukes for transferring all its perishable Tuesday foods to D-Hall during the water main break. Waste not, want not!

An irritated dart goes to EVERYONE who wastes food. I have begun working in the D-Hall dishroom and I find myself appalled at the tremendous amount of food thrown away — especially being the environmentally concerned campus we are! If you can't eat it, DON'T get it! Sent in by a concerned D-Hall employee.
To the UPB Film Committee for inviting children of faculty and staff members to the showing of "The 5,000 Fingers of Dr. 7" in the Grafton-Stovall Theatre on Saturday Oct. 19.

At this time of mid-term exams, 100-page research papers and halfway-through-the-semester stress, an apathetic dart to students who don't return library books on time. There comes a point in the semester when the two worst words in the English language are "CHECKED OUT" on Leo.
To D-Hall for turning on the heat and making dining a pleasant experience.

A careless dart to The Breeze for not checking the facts in a dart printed Oct. 17. The dart pertained to a printer supposedly stolen from Shenandoah Hall, the Office of Public Safety. The police hadn't taken over the office when the printer was stolen. The printer may have been misplaced as Math offices moved out.

To all those conscientious students who value the future enough to take on the minor inconvenience of using your R-MUG. We thank you, it does make a difference! Sent in by Resource Geography students who recognize the finite resources of our planet.
Registration over fall break? An interesting way to solve telephone registration problems.

To the long-awaited and much-appreciated opening of Lifeline. Because the line uses glassware, the only things getting dumped somewhere on Earth are paper napkins. One suggestion, though. Open the line up to the rest of D-Hall to avoid isolating those who choose to eat there from the rest of campus. Segregation does little for cross-cultural awareness.

Excuse me, but last I checked, pedestrians had the right of way, Harrisonburg rush hour or not. Most of the time, actually crossing Main Street to get to Anthony-Seeger means finally getting so fed up with the rude, speeding drivers that seem to infest our roadways that we just jump in front of them, risking life and limb to combat their complete ignorance of Driver's Ed. 101. After all, what's a lost leg when you're already late for your ethics exam? Sent in by a mass communication major with no patience and very close to no legs. But campus police are doing something to keep our legs attached - for more, see page 3.
A pat to the Steakhouse for resuming its recycling of tin cans, all aluminum and plastics. As old as the issue sounds, our planet isn't getting any younger.

To piggy students who can't keep all their food on their plates and let stuff drip all over the counters and carpet and everywhere else. OINK. Sent in by one of many yucked-out Food Services employees who spent 10 minutes on hands and knees on the floor of Pepe's scrubbing sour cream out of the carpet.
sender: one of many yucked-out Food Services employees

text: We like the Duke Dog. So there.
To the useless post-stepshow brawl threats on Friday night. Competition is one thing, violence is another.

To the long-awaited Smithereens concert Thursday. First of all, it was a good programming move on UPB's part. Second, it was a fantastic concert — and the Smithereens seems to enjoy it as much as the students did.

We just can't let this registration over fall break thing go. Could there be some sort of conspiracy with long distance telephone companies? Are they trying to make a little money off our parent's phone bills while we try to find an open section? Really, registration is traumatic enough when we're at JMU.
Well, we were all a little worried there for a while, but the Dukes' defense finally pulled through. Congrats on the strong standing in I-AA.
To whoever planned to have the Redskins game and the World Series seventh game on at exactly the same time Sunday. That must be why God made VCRs and remote controls. Ahh, the power.

And last but not least, a nostalgic pat to JMU alumni and the folks who planned homecoming this year. Alums were well-behaved, current students were too, and the activities — especially tailgating in P-lot — were awesome. Thanks to all the people who helped make this year's events so special.

A time warped dart to whoever is in charge of setting back campus clocks. In case you didn't know, Saturday was the big day to set 'em back an hour. Oh well, what difference would it make. The number of clocks on this campus that actually keep correct time are slim to none.
A pat to the new phone books. How about that pull out map and that index of street names? It may have taken a while for them to come out, but it was well worth the wait.

A belated dart to the administration for scheduling fall break so late this year. Most other schools had their breaks two weeks ago or more. We should've just tacked on the extra days with the Thanksgiving break. Now that would've been a holiday.

A heroic pat to the Office of Registration and Records for instating the new registration times for seniors who were previously held registration appointments on this Friday — fall break! Thanks for realizing the fact that most students will be long gone by that time.
target: the Office of Registration and Records

text: A naughty dart to a local bull dog named BUTCH who was witnessed maiming several small children. Yeah right!
target: a local bull dog named BUTCH

text: A pat to the creator of the "Arf" letter. It was the most insightful commentary, concerning the mascot debate, that I've seen yet! Sent in by a reader who is "dog" tired of this issue. Ba dum dum, tsss!

An unoriginal dart to Greeks that send personals using the ubiquitous phrases "You're awesome!" "Get psyched!" and "We love you." Let's use a little more creativity! Sent in by a fellow Greek who'd like to see the classified section enlivened a bit.
A thankful, very appreciative pat to the janitors and cleaning people all over campus, and especially those in Eagle Hall. You don't know just how much you mean to us! Sent in by James E. Howard.

A special thank you dart goes out to those considerate people who decided all of the bikes parked outside of the Warren Campus Center last Friday afternoon needed to be washed. And how environmentally conscious of them to simultaneously wash our bikes, water the sidewalks and the grass. Sent in by a sarcastic clean bike owner.

A candy-coated pat to the public-spirited members of the JMU cheerleaders and the men's and women's basketball teams who delayed their holiday to help kids celebrate Halloween at Valley Mall. Sent in by a grateful dad.

A ridiculous dart to whoever posted all the "wanted" signs for Christopher Columbus. It's absurd to attempt to pin the blame for all of the Americas' problems on just one person. Besides, he's been dead for 400 years. Yet another submission sent in by an opinionated James E. Howard.
A carbo-pumped pat to D-hall for the recent opening of Pasta Uno. The more variety of chow, the better.

A flaming dart to the incredibly annoying fire alarm epidemic on campus this weekend. What is the deal? Chandler, Frederickson and Eagle (surprise surprise) reported alarms. Hey, there must be some more creative way to combat boredom.
target: the incredibly annoying fire alarm epidemic

text: A recycled pat to EARTH for collecting paper cups in D-hall Friday. One problem: guilt may work wonders, but tends to develop animosity. Let's not trigger defense responses that could lead to people not recycling, period.

This may be a crazy thought, but are the Main Street crossing guards really meeting their long-term goals? Not only does their schedule seem pretty inconsistent, they aren't doing anything we couldn't do by sticking our hands out. And they don't even get to wear safety orange.
A cultural pat to the College of Fine Arts and Communication for producing a wonderful Carmen and bringing the superb Glasnost Ballet. Sent in by an appreciative Elizabeth Ihle.
target: the College of Fine Arts and Communication

text: To late-comers at cultural events such as Carmen and the Glasnost Ballet, and to the managers who delay performers to seat those late-comers. Sent in by an annoyed Elizabeth Ihle. Guess we know how Elizabeth has spent her evenings lately.
A cultural pat to the wrestling team for warring against the Russians Saturday night. Too bad we lost. But hey, what a great opportunity for everyone involved.

A cramped dart to whoever designed the stairwells in Showker Hall, the new business building. They're wide enough to accommodate about one and a half people. I don't know any half people. Sent in by an annoyed computer information systems major.
sender: an annoyed computer information systems major

text: To Pepe's for changing their guacamole. It's better without pimentos. Sent in by a pimento-hater.
To whoever threw away the recyclable items that residents had collected over the past few weeks at Madison Manor Apartments.

A convenient pat to whoever decided to purchase the stamp machine outside the bookstore. Not only does it eliminate waiting in line just for a stamp, but it also helps to decrease the length of post office lines.

A disgusting dart to the Neanderthal at the bus stop who was never taught manners. Why do men think they can spit all over campus? Believe me, women do not find this attractive or sexy; it is unhygienic, germ-ridden, and offensive. Sent in by a conscientious salivater.

A busy pat to JMU grounds keeping for their endless devotion to raking up all the leaves. Indeed, fall is one of the most beautiful times of the year, especially in the Shenandoah Valley, but somebody's gotta clean it up.

A cyanide-coated dart aimed at whoever was so inconsiderate to pull out the phone wires on Friday at a party on the second floor in Ikenberry. Just in time for registration, thanks guys. Sent in by irate Ikenberry residents.
To "The Lion and the Jewel," a play running in Theatre II, was billed by some as the best play they've seen on campus this semester.

To the water-logged sports staff — whatever happened to coverage of men's and women's swim meets? It's time you clear those fogged goggles and support the swimming Dukes! Sent in by two avid swimming fans.
An applauding pat to the voters of Louisiana. To think there was a possibility that one of America's states could be governed by a man like David Duke is scary.

Graffiti on the Greek Row bridge? Is this some sort of tribute to Prince? What a really dumb thing to do. What is the point of such barbarism? Besides, you can't even read the stuff — certainly no insightful socio-political messages here.

A thankful pat to Thanksgiving Break — it's almost here! (We're so psyched!)And that extra day (or should we say extra couple of days) will make all the difference. Now we'll have more time to sleep, eat and drink, sleep, eat and drink, sleep, eat and drink . . .

A poison-tipped dart to whomever told freshmen that extra sessions of classes would open up on the last day of registration. I’m sorry, but opening up one section of Underwater Flagpole Sitting 102 is not the slightest bit of help. Sent in by a freshman who had to register on the last day possible. Bummer.

To lesbian and gay students who speak to psychology and sociology classes, first-year dorms, English classes, etc., for putting themselves on the line to educate the masses about alternative lifestyles. Sent in by a now open-eyed student.

Just when you thought something was going right. What’s the deal? The new stamp machine only takes coins for whole stampbooks? Just pump 12 quarters, 18 dimes and 20 nickels into that sucker and you’re set.
A sympathetic pat to seniors graduating in December. It’s hardly even a ceremony, just sort of a shoving off. Oh well, look at it as a breaking-in process for the real world.

To the pig-like males who sauntered in front of Wilson Monday night yelling “rape” and blowing a whistle while laughing through their insensitive snouts. Pretty cool to be able to do all three at the same time, guys. And was the girl with you impressed? Sent in by someone who carries a whistle and respects its purpose.
Plop plop fizz fizz... thank goodness for free cold drugs at the Health Center.

To all of those nice dog owners who allow their precious cute dogs to use the campus grounds as a toilet training facility. It is hard enough to dodge the “water sprinkler show,” but to possibly land in a pile of s--t is ridiculous! Sent in by a pooper-scooper advocate.
target: all of those nice dog owners

text: An “it’s about time” pat to Hoogland (whoever he or she is) for finally giving The Breeze something funny in the comics. Too bad some people can’t take a joke — “Donut-head” is hilarious! Sent in by a frustrated Trevor the Tree Frog reader.
sender: a frustrated Trevor the Tree Frog reader

text: A down-home dart to the non-stop country music fest in Dukes. While the sappy twang is entertaining occasionally, two months is more than enough. Sent in by Elizabeth Cartwright. We know she’s really a closet Randy Travis groupie.
Congrats to the football team for making it to post-season I-AA playoffs for the second time in JMU history.

A dart to the state of Virginia for springing the budget cuts on JMU right when we thought we were in the clear. It’s pretty difficult to give back $900,000 that’s already been promised to our overworked and overwhelmed departments.

A “thank god we’ve made it” pat to every JMU student. Since we’ve made it through the faculty’s experiment to see what happens when the student body spontaneously combusts with too much work, enjoy this undoubtedly-extended Thanksgiving break. Eat, drink and be merry.

A poisonous dart to all those men out there who try to have it all by having a girlfriend (who they don’t really care about) while teasing their scopes (who they really want to be with). Sent in by someone who has obviously been suckered by some smooth-talking lady’s man.
A bountiful pat to all those who gave food and time to help with the H.O.U.S.E. Food Drive. Your efforts really made a difference!! Sent in by H.O.U.S.E.
A slacker dart to all you people who aren’t pulling your own weight on group projects — you know who you are. Sent in by someone who needs to take their project partner outside and rough ’em up.
A big pat to those who show pride in the Honor Code during exam week. Thanks. Sent in by the Duke Dog — or was that a three-eyed, antlered pig running out the door?

A childish dart to all you COLLEGE students who act like you’re in high school when eating at D-hall. I don’t understand why you can’t take up your own trays and trash or why you feel the need to unscrew the tops of the salt, pepper and sugar shakers and turn them upside down. I realize not everyone engages in these immature acts but we D-hall workers don’t get paid to clean up your uncalled-for childish messes. Sent in by a fed-up D-hall worker. Two snaps in a circle.
A holiday-spirited pat to everyone participating in Operation Santa Claus. Your actions will make some child’s Christmas.

A cyanide-filled dart to the person who wrote “KMS” on the unmarred white tile walls of the first floor women’s room in Showker. She wasn’t satisfied with it in pencil and scratched “KMS” twice more on the opposing wall. Your admission to JMU must have been an oversight, judging from your lack of intelligence. Stay out of restrooms, use a mud puddle — it suits you better. Signed, “an obviously more intelligent individual.” Ouch.
A patient pat to the entire student body for enduring the first few grueling days of the semester. Just think, this time next week your head probably will have stopped spinning.
A sour scrooge dart to the jerks who destroyed the Christmas tree in Garber before break. Nice holiday spirit! What’s next? Snaring the Easter Bunny?
A pat to JM’s for surviving the mob of thirsty students attending Ladies’ Night Tuesday. Everyone and their sister showed up!
To whoever decided to give Paula Abdul a star on Hollywood Boulevard at the same time as Jimi Hendrix. It took him 20 years, and it took her two albums. Sent in by Scott Surovell.

Ah hell, why not? A pat to everyone else at JMU (faculty, employees, etc.) for enduring the first few grueling days of student whining — “We just want to graduate!” (to be read in the spoiled, whiny tone of a third grader).

To an administration that has found the funds to hire a Provost at $90,000 a year for a college that doesn’t exist, but can do nothing about giving well-deserved raises to underpaid, overworked staff; or improving the library; or improving housing. First things first — let’s improve and take care of what we already have! Leave the dreams for better financial times. Sent in by a student concerned with JMU’s present, not future.

A victorious pat to the men’s gymnastics team for defeating Cornell and Radford and breaking the school record for the highest total points scored in a meet. And to the women’s team for defeating Cornell and Rutgers. Go tumblin’ Dukes!
An inaccessible dart to those professors who are never in their offices and don’t even have answering machines! It’s difficult to get to know a professor if he or she is impossible to track down.
And appropriately, a courteous pat to those professors who do have answering machines and return student calls promptly.

A reject dart to all the mindless idiots who took it upon themselves to make the Policelog in the last issue of The Breeze a full page and a half of embarrassment. Come on people, we’re college students, not criminals.
A pat to everyone who threw a party the first official weekend back at school. You all are the true movers and motivators of JMU’s student social life.
A moronic dart to the designer of the new sweatshirts in the bookstore that read "JMU University." Get a clue!
An impressive pat to Coach Sheila Moorman for grabbing her 200th win in JMU women's basketball. Keep it up!
An inflationary dart to whoever decided to jack the price of P.C. Duke's potato chips up 10 cents. What'll be jacked up next, tuition? Nah, that could never happen.

An assertive pat to the SGA for their letter-writing campaign concerning budget cuts in higher education. But remember, the only way their assertiveness will pay off is if the student body participates.

An incosiderate dart to all the local train engineers who decide to check the reverse gears on their engines while blocking the railroad crossing behind Anthony-Seeger. Actually, we know it's necessary for taking care of train "things," but seeing an engineer with his head out the window, looking backwards and saying "wheeee" is enough to make anyone snap while waiting to cross.

A patient pat to the residents of Wine-Price, Hillside, and the Village for dealing with the daily noise of bulldozers and dump trucks. The new addition to the campus center may be nice once it's done, but until then - beep, beep.

A dart of impropriety to university calendar planners who don't think the celebration of Dr. Martin Luther King Jr.'s birthday is reason enough to have the day free of classes. Too many people will have to miss the activities planned for the afternoon and evening. When the majority of states in this country believe it is important enough to shut down their governments, where does that put JMU?
A safety and convenience pat to the new paved and lit path to the Convo by University Boulevard. No more treacherous treading to basketball games at night.
target: the new paved and lit path

text: A sniffling, sneezing dart to the combination of germs and crappy weather that has made all of us tissue-laden balls of flu. If one more hacking student snuffles during a quiz, we quit.

A healthy hearty trimming pat to the just open Wellness Center in Godwin. The brand-spanking-new facility has some great machines (even if they look like medieval torture devices) to work just about any conceivable body part to exhaustion. It even smells okay (so far).

Not that we get any mail anyway, but this closed campus center deal really put a pucker in the hope-filled eyes of everyone who checks two, three, seven times a day to make sure their boxes are really empty. And moving all those meetings was a confusing drag.
A pat to the Council of Campus Leaders for its presentations during Human Relations Week. The mind-opening lectures, discussions and workshops gave us all a lot to think about.

To all the bandwagon anti-Redskin fans who suddenly emerge from the woodwork to pronounce their hatred. I'm surprised you haven't picked yourself up any Bills attire yet. Sent in by an anonymous 'Skins groupie with an apparently low tolerance for diversity.
A commendable pat to the Martin Luther King, Jr. formal ceremony committee for their coordination of a touching program on Monday—respectful, moving and unforgettable, just as it should have been.
target: the Martin Luther King, Jr. formal ceremony committee

text: Hey, how long can that door to the post office of the Warren Campus Center stay broken? Sent in by someone who swears it has been under repair for at least three years now. Careful with the complaints, though. That may not be true; and if it's not, they may shut down the post office again just to torture us.

A pat of selflessness and generosity to all who sent in personals commemorating Dr. King and Leann Whitlock. The ads raised about $150 for the Whitlock scholarship. More pats also, to those who donated to the fund after the MLK presentation.

A lazy dart to that annoying pack of imbeciles who insist on waiting for the elevator in the campus center and blocking the halls in the process. The elevators are for handicapped students. Use the stairs, you bums.

A social activism pat to the students who believe in issues strongly enough to defend them publicly, passively. Though your views may differ, or even if you find their views sometimes offensive, they deserve some credit for exercising the rights guaranteed by the First Amendment.

A dart to all of us for allowing our world to revolve around the Super Bowl. Yeah, it's not your ordinary football game, but the way we're all acting, if game day was during the week classes would be cancelled.
A heroic pat to Mr. Richard Dewey for taking it upon himself to lead the rescue of an epileptic victim in Showker Hall Saturday afternoon!
But a slacker dart to the city of Harrisonburg for taking so long to get the snow plows out! Cars were sliding all over the road, people were stranded and pissed off!
To the Contemporary Gospel Singers, who, on Monday night, made even the angels stop singing and listen. What amazing, God-given and God-acknowledged talent—AMEN!

A foolish dart to anyone who is a racist. There is absolutely no justification for human beings to treat one another like dirt, especially if one group or culture does not know much of anything about another and develops idiotic prejudices based on oftentimes ridiculous stereotypes. Sent in by Roland Massa.

A pat to the Council of Campus Leaders for their efforts in creating Human Relations Week. In particular the PRIME Workshop was the most powerful part of the week. I hope students will take advantage of PRIME and learn about not only others but also themselves. Sent in by Brian J. Zarahn.

An exhaust-choking dart to any inconsiderate bus drivers who gleefully watch students run screaming toward a bus, then take off just when they're about to reach the door. I can still see the gleam in their eyes in the rear view mirror and hear their evil cackles as they pull off in a cloud of dust. Just wait a few seconds! Sent in by a student who claims to have flicked off over 50 drivers. Who knows, it may have been the same driver 50 times. Maybe if you'd stop giving him the finger, he'd wait.

A pat to all the students who volunteer to do CARS, a CCM-sponsored service that operates on Thursday, Friday and Saturday nights driving people safely home from parties. A special pat to Chris and Katrine who drove for four hours straight in the ice and snow. Sent in by a thankful (warm, safe) student.
An unnatural dart to whoever removed the trees near the Bluestone area basketball court to make room for yet another building project.

A spirited pat to the faithful Dukes fans who attend the basketball games consistently. But don't neglect the women's team, they're dribbling their tails off too—Sunday at 2 p.m. they play a key game against Richmond.
A fashion dart to all Redskin fans. The hideous maroon cursive "R" hat is the ugliest in the NFL. Sent in by anti-Skins fans who think the Super Bowl was played on Nov. 24—against Dallas.
Here's to being one-fourth of the way through the semester, halfway through the block, but nowhere near finals.
target: being one-fourth of the way through the semester

text: An inconvenient dart to parking for not installing, oh, just a wee-little parking space or two up next to D-hall so that students driving to the "Money Machine" don't have to park on the sidewalk. You know how it is... leaving the flashers on while you sprint up to the machine and bite your nails in hopes that no campus police cars drive by—too much stress!

An intelligent pat to Steve Daisey for his excellent letter in the Jan. 27 Breeze. I wonder if John Lofton's relatives gave their lives to help defeat the narrow-minded Nazis, who, by the way, killed several million Jews during WWII. Called in by a concerned citizen.

A strangely-scheduled dart to those in charge of the 92 Days to Graduation Party for throwing the celebration on Monday night. Friday was the 92nd day until graduation, in case someone wasn't counting. And what about the seniors who want to cheer the Dukes to a win over UR?
To the campus grounds crew for putting gravel over the annoying mud pits surrounding the sidewalks behind Anthony-Seeger.

A brain-dead dart to all the meatheads who stand their big burly selves at the door of an off-campus party and assault newcomers with the words, "You got a buck?" Sent in by someone who wanted no beer but was still verbally attacked by some thug with a single-digit IQ.
A spic-and-span pat to JMU's cleaning staff for keeping all the buildings on campus looking so nice. Thanks!
A dart in triplicate to the Records office for giving the already overworked seniors the privileged task of filling out a monstrous graduation application! Sent in by a triple fed-up senior.
An appreciative pat to UPB for sponsoring Odadaa. "Let the music begin" again! Sent in by a student who went into Wilson Hall depressed and came out dancing.

A not so clever dart to the student who parked her car in extended A-lot behind Gibbons last week, stuck a previously issued parking ticket under her windshield wiper, and walked on her merry way. Sent in by a staff member in search of a parking place who notified a nearby campus police officer to issue a second ticket. These COLLEGE students think they're so smart...
sender: a staff member in search of a parking place

text: Hey, come to think of it, those bus drivers who keep on schedule deserve a pat. After all, if they waited for every tardy, bus-chasing student, we'd never get anywhere.

A didn't-your-mother-ever-teach-you-anything dart to everyone who, upon receiving mass mailing flyers in the Post Office, just throws them down on the floor and steps all over them. What makes you think the housekeeping staff has nothing better to do than sweep up your unwanted poster sale announcements? That must be why there are three, count 'em, three trash cans right there in the Post Office.
A light-bright pat to the lighting erected on the Hillside field for students circumventing the campus center construction by night.
A fire-hazard dart to the lobotomized morons who put empty coffee pots back on the burner in D-Hall, then sniff dumbly, wondering what that smell is. Duh.

A warm-hearted pat to the outstanding "Toon into JMU" conference hosted by the Student Ambassadors. What a tremendous success! Sent in by a collection of impressed administrators from University Advancement and Admissions.
sender: a collection of impressed administrators from University Advancement and Admissions

text: A smelly, cancerous dart to the person who always fills the Anthony Seeger upstairs bathroom with smoke. Whenever I go there during class, my teachers think I left class to smoke. Sent in by a frequent, non-smoking, mirror user.

And by the way, a hefty pat to PC Dukes for cooking enough pizza to feed the more than 400 Student Ambassador delegates lunch Friday. Who knows, maybe a world record was set for the most pizza consumed at one time.
A pat of generosity to all those people who share their time doing community service. It means so much to so many. Sent in by Bethany Callard, a member of service fraternity Alpha Phi Omega.

A thoughtless dart to the Krissy Heinbaugh basketball caption last Monday. Obviously the writer was more concerned with her game-tying miss than with the lead she gained for the Dukes earlier in the game. Sent in by junior Heidi Yancey, who knows Heinbaugh will help the Dukes far more than she would ever hurt them.

A dart of damnation to the anal-retentive thief who stole some CDs at a keg party last weekend. Sent in by an angry CD-collector who would like to have parties and have an ounce of trust in fellow Dukes.
A warm and hearty thank you pat to Food Services at D-Hall for providing newspapers for us faithful breakfasters.

An annoyed dart to the JMU police officer who completely ignored the pedestrian yield light in front of Anthony-Seeger as I was crossing the street. It's bad enough nobody else stops, but come on! Sent in by pedestrian Cathi Stillman.
A connecting pat to the Vax system, which lets students all across the country communicate through Internet/Bitnet mail. We can "talk" to any campus with the same system, at no charge.

A dart to all the professors with attendance policies. It seems strange to me that we spend thousands of dollars to go to school here, yet we're not allowed to sleep in and miss an occasional class. Our money, our choice, right? I feel like I'm still in high school. I just hope you guys don't start calling my mommy. Sent in by Mike Nicolosi.
An understanding pat to the campus police for straightening out a student's ticket problem quickly and courteously. Sent in by a justly mis-parked commuter student.

To Dan Konnor for his article in Madison Review condemning the JMU's anti-discrimination clause concerning "sexual orientation." As a lesbian and particularly as a Christian, I am appalled that he's overlooked "Thou shalt not judge." My girlfriend and I will see you in heaven Dan. Signed happy, holy and homosexual.
A sincere pat to the folks responsible for the much improved cycle by-pass at the Newman Avenue gate. This should encourage more students to ride. Sent in by James H. Saker, a close neighbor.
To the cartoonist who draws "Donut-Head." Who is he and does anyone besides you think he is funny? I'd laugh more at the obituaries if The Breeze had any. Sent in by Philip Kim.
To Swervyn Mervyn, the hippest DJ on WXJM, whose show "The Reagan Years" (Wed. nights 11-1 p.m.) lets us relive those fond memories of junior high. Sent in by an avid fan, obviously.

A dart to whoever decided to keep residence halls open until 3 p.m. on Saturday at the beginning of spring break. Resident advisors and hall directors want to get out of here just as much (probably more!) as everyone else. Sent in by an irritated RA.

A safety-conscience pat to the increasing number of professors who are allowing bad weather policies for commuter students. Getting to class is hardly worth risking your life—but on second thought, death probably would guarantee you an excused absence.

To the whiny R.A.'s who complain of having to stay an additional 22 hours over spring break. U. of R. is probably our biggest game of the year and the Dukes need our support. Where's your school spirit? Or are you only a loyal student when you're being paid for it? Sent in by an R.A. who thinks that keeping the halls open was a great idea—and who volunteered to sit duty that weekend.

A-thank-you-for-doing-what-you-say-you-will pat to all professors who actually keep their posted office hours and don't use that time to run to the cleaners, drug store, nearby planets, etc., while students wait (with their fingers up their noses) for hours outside their offices.

A litter-laden dart to Student Ambassadors for putting purple and gold paw prints all over the sidewalks for their conference, and to this day not cleaning them up. Sent in by a senior who learned to clean up after herself in nursery school.
To the safety-conscious persons responsible for installing the nifty new emergency phones all over campus. Now help (not to mention someone with keys to the dorm) is a dial away!

A misinformed dart to the Jan. 16 Breeze article which stated that only one member of the Greek community participated in the Men of Madison calendar. Craig Honeycutt, lead singer of Everything, "February," is a brother of Alpha Kappa Lambda. Sent in by a Greek Woman of Madison.
To The Breeze for printing the Feb. 17 "What we love about JMU" article. We didn't know you cared! Sent in by Food Services.
A thoughtless dart to the bastard(s) in Weaver Hall who find it necessary to supplement their wealth by stealing money and belongings of others. Sent in by a disgruntled victim of petty larceny.
sender: a disgruntled victim of petty larceny

text: To the "Special Greeks" for the wonderful luncheon they had for us Feb. 19. Everything was so good and greatly appreciated. You all are more than students, you're friends. Also thanks to the special girls who donated blood for our housekeeper, Mary Breeden, who has had a lengthy illness. Sent in by Linda Miller and the rest of the housekeeping crew who work on "the Row."
sender: Linda Miller and the rest of the housekeeping crew

text: A dart to whoever calls the shots in Carrier Library. Closing the library at 10 p.m. on Friday and Saturday nights is an insult to JMU's accreditation as a major public university. The 30 or so students who were rounded up and herded out of the library Friday night serve as proof that some students use part of their weekends to study. Sent in by a pissed-off, weekend library goer.
To the JMU Campus Cadets for working late every night to provide escorts and enhance the safety of the JMU community. Sent in by a student who is tired of all the "Cadet Bashing."
A wake-the-dead dart to the noisy bus brakes that awaken us every morning. Sent in by a group of sleepy Village residents.
sender: a group of sleepy Village residents

text: To the construction workers who are expanding the WCC and bettering our campus. Sent in by four seniors.

A customer-is-always-right dart to any workers in JMU customer service offices (i.e., the Post Office, Health Center, Records Office, etc.) who refuse to acknowledge the person standing at the counter whistling "William Tell" for five minutes while they finish world-important conversations about nothing. Sent in by a student who apparently had a sign saying "please ignore me" on her forehead all day.

To Dr. Carrier for coming down to our Happy Hour last Friday. We really enjoyed hanging out with you. Thanks for supporting the Greek system here at JMU and giving us a place where all Greeks have the opportunity to live together. Sent in by Chi Phi Fraternity.

A mean ol' dart to the Duke Dog for only sporadically appearing at the women's basketball games. Some community children come to games just to see the big furry guy. Sent in by someone who has seen sad eyes.

To IFC, Alpha Phi Omega, EARTH and all the other organizations who participated in the Newman Lake clean-up on Saturday. A special thanks to those who actually got into the lake to fish out TVs, grills, etc. From Danny Cruce, chair of lake clean-up.
target: IFC, Alpha Phi Omega, EARTH and all the other organizations

text: A smoking dart to those who flick their butts on the grass. Smoking may affect you, but littering affects everybody. The abundance of butts around campus is unsightly. Have some consideration for those who like to lie in the grass and dispose of them properly.
Yeah it's here! Have a safe break and come back with all your limbs and at least enough brain cells to last until graduation.

To the removal of most, if not all, of the ash trays (urns, canisters) from the entrances to campus buildings, making it impossible for a considerate smoker to dispose of a cigarette "properly." Believe it or not, most of us don't enjoy being litter bugs! Sent in by a smoker who wants to do the right thing.

To the Dukes for their 21-win season so far and to Lefty Driesell for his 600 career wins. Hopefully they'll get the NCAA at-large bid. If not, we can definitely look forward to a good showing in the NIT.

A frustrated dart to that kind student who hit my car while backing out of Z Lot the week before break. Accidents happen, but it would be nice if you owned up to them. Sent in by someone too mad to be witty.

A thank you pat to the students who donated their spaghetti-o's, cream of broccoli soup, macaroni and cheese and other foods to the food drive on Feb. 27. We collected 1,269.1 pounds of food from the JMU apartment complexes. Blessed Sacrament Food Pantry was thrilled! Sent in by Housing Opportunities Uniting Students and Educators (H.O.U.S.E.), a homeless advocacy group.
sender: Housing Opportunities Uniting Students and Educators

text: A lazy dart to all those who refuse to have their IDs re-magnetized and hold up the line at D-Hall. Sent in by two annoyed cashiers.
To the JV and varsity women's fencing teams for their first place wins at State. Congratulations to those who placed in individuals, too. A fencing fan.
target: the JV and varsity women's fencing teams

text: A dart to the schmuck who scheduled assessments on the day after St. Patty's Day. Oh what a sight — thousands of hung over seniors trying to focus and take themselves seriously.

A special pat to all of those caring people who braved the horrendous sight and smell to take care of and clean up after a friend who experienced the unequaled thrill and pleasure of "worshipping the porcelain god." Sent in by a poor, unfortunate soul (with great friends) who worshipped that evil, false god... and missed.
sender: a poor, unfortunate soul (with great friends)

text: To all JMU office workers who answer the phone by saying "Hello" and not identifying their office or themselves. Sent in by someone who likes formalities.

A huge wet pat to the Bad Boys of Madison for bringing home the gold. Not only did the men's swimming and diving team win the CAA championship, they beat the all-time high score! Way to go Dukes! Sent in by the same two avid swim fans.
sender: the same two avid swim fans

text: To all those fashion slaves who display their narrow-minded ignorance by ridiculing people who wear both the straps of their bookbag. In the midst of a national recession and racial violence it's promising to see people are so concerned that I'm wearing both straps. Pardon the faux pas, but if I wanted to wear one strap I would've bought a one-strapped book bag. Call me a rebel, but I'll continue to be a dedicated double-strapper. Sent in by Bart Donlan.
A conservationist pat to D-Hall for switching to glassware in Line 5. Sent in by a student with a conscience.

An out-to-lunch dart to the Records office for closing down from 12 p.m. until 1 p.m. every day. People in every other office on campus (in the country for that matter) eat lunch, but they see fit to eat in shifts instead of shutting down the entire operation. Right before or after lunch is the perfect time for students to stop in, not the perfect time to be closed.
To the student ambassadors for hosting Special Visitation Day for prospective students. Leading hundreds of high school seniors around campus is a task not many of us would be willing to take on.

A bumbling dart to The Breeze for incorrectly replacing the phrase "conservation of energy" with "conversion of energy" in my letter to the editor. If it ain't broke, don't fix it! Sent in by Greg Gingerich.
To the professors and students who are both interested and willing to speak out regarding issues on the future of James Madison and the New College of Integrated Science and Technology.

A sexist dart to the person(s) responsible for the signs on the rest room door at Entrance 5, Gibbons. Flowers on the women's sign imply that women are delicate (i.e., weak) and an eagle holding a flag on the men's sign implies that men are patriotic (i.e., strong). Sent in by two individuals who do not think this is a trivial complaint.
A wake-up-early-to-take-a-test pat to the sophomores and seniors who took the assessment tests while everyone else "came to" at noon.

To Pi Kappa Phi for their PUSH Week fundraising methods. The cause is great — but why a competition between the sororities on Greek Row? All fraternities and sororities, as well as many other organizations at JMU, should be involved. Sent in by two Greek women PUSHing for campus unity.
sender: two Greek women PUSHing for campus unity

text: A real cool pat to WXJM for sponsoring Cool Aid, a unique showcase of JMU bands that benefited Mercy House. And much thanks to Johnnies Heritage, Succotash, the Dave Matthews Band, Cillia, Dancecrashers and the Cicada for contributing their talent.
To the granola-eating, shower-boycotting, Earth mug-carrying, hackey-sacking, mascot-changing SGA candidates. Sent in by two extremely opinionated students concerned with the future of JMU.
target: the granola-eating, shower-boycotting, Earth mug-carrying, hackey-sacking, mascot-changing SGA candidates

text: A pat to President and Mrs. Carrier for the invitations cordially inviting all the students participating in the Emerging Leaders program to a reception at Oakview April 1.
To those thumping speakers in P.C. Dukes. What a pleasant atmosphere to chow down in... what?... huh?... speak up, I can't hear you! Sent in by a student who likes to hear himself chew.
A community-service pat to everyone who volunteered their time for the Very Special Arts program which took place in the P.C. Ballroom Friday.

A brain-dead dart to all the zombies who are oblivious to the fact that standing in the middle of the WCC hallways to socialize might block traffic. Flick your cerebral switch on and get the hell out of the way! Sent in by a student who has resorted to body checking these thoughtless punks.

A great big pat for the members of JMU's Animal Rights Coalition protesting the use of donkeys in a "donkey basketball" game at Broadway High School. Animals were not put on this Earth to be abused. Sent in by a concerned individual.

An unsanitary dart to the people who "taste-test" the D-Hall food straight from the buffet with their fingers. Who taught you manners? Sent in by a student who doesn't think "finger-licking good" means scum from someone else's finger.
To the women in Records who patiently help us at registration in Wine-Price. And to the women at the counter in Wilson Hall — thanks! Sent in by an appreciative individual.

A dart to all computer lab assistants who, through no fault but theirs, lost my entire document while attempting to load spell check to my disk! Thanks! By the way, saying "ooops, I'm sorry" is no consolation. Sent in by someone who spent three hours typing their paper and three hours trying to recover it — but never did.
A way-to-go pat to Kembrew McLeod and Phil Sweeney for motivating some usually lazy types into at least thinking about voting. Sent in by a grad student who would have voted if policy would allow.

To The Breeze for making errors in my March 26 letter to the editor. The message I was trying to convey was that "I don't ever want to have to choose between my black friends or white friends." Sent in by an annoyed Katie Whitaker.
A cross-your-fingers-and-hope-it-continues pat to the great telephone God for allowing registration to continue without a major disaster.

A flaming dart to all the boring, complacent, unquestioning, apathetic, narrow-minded, society-living, styrofoam-using, Top 40 listening packrats that infest this campus. Sent in by a verbose, opinionated, active, analytical, open-minded, Earth mug-using student!!!
target: all the boring, complacent, unquestioning, apathetic, narrow-minded, society-living, styrofoam-using, Top 40 listening packrats
sender: a verbose, opinionated, active, analytical, open-minded, Earth mug-using student!!!

text: To minority outreach for sponsoring the black freshman weekend that brings a ton of prospective students to JMU every year. JMU can use all the diversity it can get.

A shameful dart to The Breeze SGA reporter, who I remind you is supposed to be politically independent while on duty, who supported Alexis McCombs by wearing an Alexis McCombs pin. Sent in by an angry anti-Alexis McCombs supporter.

To the Democratic voters of Connecticut for catapulting Jerry Brown into the national media and keeping the race for the nomination wide open. A Bush-Clinton race in August is liable to keep a lot of voters wondering who is the lesser of two evils.

To those who have used this forum for the past two issues to whine and call each other names. If you can't even tolerate each other here, how do you plan to deal with people you don't agree with when you leave this little world? Sent in anonymously.
And many thanks to the janitorial staff of Wine-Price for keeping our hall spotless... Sent in by Kristi Graves.

A didn't-your-mom-ever-tell-you dart to all those who choose to drive on the sidewalks. Building and Grounds has a valid reason for using these paths, but wanting to get where you are going faster is not a valid reason. And barreling down a sidewalk at warp speed tends to be dangerous for pedestrians trying to use the sidewalk as it was intended.

A well-deserved pat to "all computer lab assistants who, through no fault but theirs" have done an outstanding job helping students and faculty in the labs. Keep up the good work! Sent in by the student lab managers.

To the JMU administration for not having a Caucasian, Alaskan native, Jewish, American Indian, Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Indian, Spanish American, etc., Freshman Weekend. I think you get the idea. Sent in by a collective group of freshmen who feel they would have benefitted tremendously from a special weekend for their respective backgrounds.

An it-is-about-time pat to the United Nations Security Council for giving Libyan leader Moammar Gadhafi until April 15 to turn over six suspected terrorists. The United States has spent enough time trying to keep Libya in line. It is about time someone else tries.

A shame-on-you dart to all the "apathetic, narrow-minded, Top-40 listening packrats" and the "shower-boycotting, Earth-mug-using, tree huggers" for resorting to name-calling. Correct me if I'm wrong, but aren't we in college now? Perhaps you should use your energy for more constructive activities, such as solving problems on campus together. Remember, a house divided cannot stand. Sent in anonymously.
target: all the "apathetic, narrow-minded, Top-40 listening packrats" and the "shower-boycotting, Earth-mug-using, tree huggers"

text: To those who participated in the Academic Computer Fair in the Convocation Center last Thursday. It's good to know that in the days of budget cuts and tuition hikes, some people at the university are still looking ahead to the next century.

A money-laundering dart to probably the highest paid campus police force in the country. How, pray tell, do you spend $191,000 on parking lot maintenance? Y'all got a better racket going than the bookstore. Sent in by Robert Rayfield and Will Acree.
target: probably the highest paid campus police force

text: To the university for pushing back the fall calendar by one week. Now we don't have to come back to the sweltering August heat quite as early. Who knows — the change might even push our spring break back a week so that it actually begins in March. Imagine that!

An annoying dart to the procrastinating students who catch an attitude with the media resource staff at the library when the microfilm/microfiche copiers jam or break down. We do our best to fix them; we're not hired for our mechanical abilities! Sent in by a student who spent three hours filing microfiche, helping ignorant students who obviously didn't do their Library Skills Workbook, and attempting to fix copiers designed and made in foreign countries, all at once.
To JMU's social fraternities and sororities for putting on a humorous, entertaining Greek Sing, a JMU tradition that is going to be here for a long time.

To anyone who oppresses free speech by removing and destroying fliers for events that they don't support. Let others decide for themselves what they want to read. Sent in by a student who is killing more trees than she would like to.
To Interfaith Campus Ministries for sponsoring a Holocaust remembrance service to reflect on the significance of the Holocaust and remember those who acted to protect the innocent and victimized.

A "didn't your mother raise you better than that" dart to the inconsiderate people who are so LAZY that they tromp through flowerbeds and wear paths across the grass, instead of using the sidewalks. C'mon folks — is it really worth ruining the beauty of our campus just to save a few steps? Sent in anonymously.
To First Right for sponsoring the Right to Life Week. Regardless of whether you agree or disagree with its position, it deserves praise for promoting thought and dispelling apathy among JMU students.
An uninformed dart to The Breeze for its ignorance on the difference between theater and theatre. One watches a movie in a theater, while a play is presented in a theatre. Sent in by a theatre major.

To Sigma Nu fraternity for taking time out last Saturday morning to work at the 10-mile Walk-A-Thon for multiple sclerosis. They worked registration, stood in the snow, provided food and water at the rest station and helped deliver pizza after we worked up an appetite. Thanks! Sent in by two walkers who enjoyed Sigma Nu's friendliness.
To the SGA for funding a lobbying group in Washington, D.C., rather than a literary magazine at JMU. Sent in by some first floor residents in Hoffman Hall.

A polite pat to the males on campus who still offer to hold the door, pick up the tab and let their date in the car first (to name a few examples) — in spite of negative feminist attitudes which seem so prevalent. Lots of us women still appreciate a man who is a gentleman! Sent in anonymously.

A really annoying dart to whoever decided to "plant" more of those post and chain contraptions across campus to prevent students from walking across the grass. What good is plush green grass when you can't walk, play or otherwise frolic through it?

A big THANK YOU pat goes out to all the people who made donations to the National Multiple Sclerosis Society on our behalf. From your generosity, we were able to raise $365.19 for the Super Cities Walk. We could not have done it without you! Thanks again for the great support. Sent in by the 1992 field hockey team.
sender: your generosity, we were able to raise $365

text: A soggy dart to those who are planning graduation for not providing an alternate location in case of rain and even telling graduates that they can't use umbrellas if a downpour does occur while they are sitting in the middle of the field.

To the members of the predominately black Greek letter organization for all the community service work that we do that sometimes seems to go unrecognized by our peers. Though we are service organizations and we do things to give back to the community, it's nice to know that we are appreciated. Sent in by Rhonda Cunningham, a member of the Sigma Gamma Rho Sorority Inc.

To those students who eat in line three and are too good to clear their own places. We don't get paid to bus tables, so if you insist on leaving trash, trays, cups, etc. on the tables, then please leave a tip. Sent in by Angela Deck, D-hall employee.

A tremendous pat to the National Hockey League owners and players' union for resolving their disputes, ending the players' strikes, and getting on with the hockey season. Now the Rangers can finally commence with their Stanley Cup venture. Sent in by a lifetime Ranger fan who will also relish in the Capital's imminent demise.
target: the National Hockey League owners and players' union

text: To all the impolite, inconsiderate students who disrespectfully leave lectures early when a professor or guest speaker is in the middle of his/her speech. If you are not interested, don't come! Have some empathy for others, please. Sent in by a student who has had an HCOM class and appreciates the role of lectures.

A polite pat to all PEOPLE on campus who still offer to hold the door, pick up the tab and let their date in the car first (to name a few examples) — in spite of sexist attitudes which seem so prevalent. Lots of people still appreciate courtesy on the part of both sexes. Sent in by Shawna Densmore and Amy Wan.

To the stadium for playing obnoxiously loud music over the PA system early Sunday morning for field hockey practice. We appreciate the need for entertainment but you disturbed the Lake area, the Row and the surrounding community. Next time, bring a box. Sent in by the Alpha Sigma Tau house.

An appreciative pat to the many self-respecting women on campus who would rather take responsibility for themselves than be doted on by some crave, pandering "gentlemen." As one of the many guys on campus who prefers having a woman as an equal partner to having a "lady" as a dependent, I give you my respect and thanks. Sent in anonymously.

A searing dart to the grand poobah in the sky who has decided that one door to the campus center must remain broken for the rest of existence. The "PLEASE USE OTHER DOOR" sign has been on that broken door for at least an eternity. If you can renovate an entire bookstore and post office over the summer, the least you could do is fix a single door.

To the Student Ambassadors for providing a much needed service: information for lost/bewildered students. Their information table on the steps of Wilson Hall over the last few days was not only a bright idea but also greatly appreciated by those a little overwhelmed by all this new-school stuff.

A much-ado-about-nothing dart to the relocation of Mr. Chips to the old police building. The relocation has added little to the service that the store provides for the students (besides those pretty neon signs cropping up everywhere this year). Furthermore, its new location is more inconvenient for everyone but those who live in the Village.

To those new gripper steps on the stairs near P.C. Dukes. At least now students won't slip on the stairs when they are coated with the mysterious grease/water that rains down on those who use the stairs.

A downright stupid dart to the idiot(s) that plastered "Free Charles Manson" posters around the campus. Freedom of expression is one thing, but exhibiting identifiable use of brainpower is quite another. GET A LIFE! Sent in by junior Roger Decker.

To those involved in the Wine-Price open house on Tuesday. Since most of the temporary student leadership offices are now located there, an opportunity to find the new offices (and eat cotton candy) was welcome.

A big, fat dart to the SGA for their negligent actions on Thursday, Sept. 3. No SGA members had opened the book sale drop off at the appointed time of 9 a.m. When you have classes from 9:25 until after 4 p.m., 9 a.m. is the only time you can drop off books. Lugging around extra, unwanted textbooks all day is terribly inconvenient and the SGA's actions were highly irresponsible. We elected you because we thought you were the best people to fill your positions. Maybe you should start doing your jobs. Sent in anonymously.
A musical pat to the UPB and WXJM for sponsoring the FREE Ocean Blue concert last Thursday. JMU students are always looking for anything free they can get their hands on.

A gravel-filled, dust storm dart to the parking committee for taking S-lot away from the students. Now students must wake up at the crack of dawn and circle like vultures just to find a space in the gravel pit — the only parking lot located on upper campus.
To the Nielsen Construction Company, Inc. for bequeathing Ashby and Converse residents $25 gift certificates to the JMU bookstore for the inconvenience caused by its construction.

A sweltering dart to the designers of the registration hell students endured over the past week. Students, not to mention the workers, had to deal with scathing heat and long lines just to pick up a couple classes. There has got to be another way.

A pat of gratitude goes out to all the student organizations, student staff and individuals who directed traffic, unloaded cars, answered questions, and got everyone moved into their residence halls. Your efforts were VERY appreciated by parents, classmates and the office of residence life. Sent in by Jim McConnel, director of the office of residence life.
target: all the student organizations, student staff and individuals

text: A mystery dart to the disappearing ride board in the Warren Campus Center. The ride board is a necessary convenience for all those wishing to escape the community of Harrisonburg on the weekends. If we could only get those meddling kids to get on this case, we might get to the bottom of this...

To the workers at Entrance 6 who directed and endured thousands of grumpy, hot students who were seeking meal plans, new IDs, etc. If it were not for the long hours they put in, the wait would have been even longer.

A hot and sweaty dart to the UPB for cramming 500 people into the hot gym with no chairs and no air conditioning — when it was beautiful outside. The Ocean Blue would have sounded much better under the sun, with the grass under our feet.

A tasty pat to P.C. Dukes for trying out some new alternatives, as well as reorganizing the food arrangement. Whoever coined the phrase "variety is the spice of life" must be working for Dukes right now.

An inconvenience dart to those responsible for requiring students to trek to the Convocation Center during certain hours over a three-day period to have their IDs validated. Isn't that what the campus card center or Entrance 6 at D-Hall is for?
A musical pat to the Marching Royal Dukes who earned the right to play at Sunday's Redskins game during halftime. Good luck — break a leg.
